page.h1: HTS Chapter 29: Organic Chemicals — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: Tariffs on U.S. Organic Chemicals by Market (HTS Ch. 29) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What the EU, Mexico, Canada, China, Japan and India charge on U.S. organic chemicals and drug ingredients, by market and product, with each market's chemical-registration rules.

intro: Tariffs are low or zero for most of this chapter's biggest markets: the EU (since July 1, 2026, except mannitol and sorbitol), Mexico, Canada and South Korea charge nothing on qualifying U.S. chemicals, while Japan, Brazil, India and Türkiye charge MFN rates. China is the exception, adding a flat 10% on top of its MFN rates. What usually decides access is chemical registration — REACH in the EU, K-REACH in Korea, KKDIK in Türkiye, Order No. 12 in China — and, for drug ingredients, the medicines regulator; each market's regulator is listed below.

assumptions: MFN rates are the World Bank/UNCTAD WITS (TRAINS) simple-average applied rates for one representative six-digit subheading per heading — the subheading with the largest 2025 U.S. exports in that heading (for example 2937.19 for hormones and 2901.10 for saturated acyclic hydrocarbons) — for the most recent year WITS holds (2019–2023). National 8–10-digit lines can differ, and many pharmaceutical ingredients are duty-free in the sample.
USMCA (Mexico, Canada) and KORUS (South Korea) apply 0% to qualifying U.S.-origin goods; the normal-rate column shows each market's MFN rate for goods that do not qualify.

For the EU, Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 zeroes out Chapter 29 from July 1, 2026 to December 31, 2029, except mannitol (2905 43) and sorbitol (2905 44); the normal-rate column shows the rate the EU charged before then.

China's cells add the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods to its MFN rate. China's 2019 counter-tariffs on U.S. goods, valid unless a line is covered by an exclusion until December 31, 2026, are not added because exclusions are granted line by line. Three Chapter 29 lines (mannitol, sorbitol, glycerol) are on China's Board of Trade list, with no published tariff cut.

India's rates are the basic customs duty only; surcharges and IGST are not included, and the February 2026 U.S.–India framework has not been implemented as far as we found. Brazil, Japan and Türkiye show MFN rates.
